v0.label: cement
v0.why: ‘Cement relations’ means to strengthen them — a positive action.

v1.label: cultivate
v1.why: ‘Cultivate relationships’ means to actively develop them — a positive action.

v2.label: cut off
v2.why: ‘Cut off relations’ means to end them abruptly — a negative action.

v3.label: damage
v3.why: ‘Damage relations’ means to harm them — a negative action.

v4.label: develop
v4.why: ‘Develop relations’ means to grow them — a positive action.

v5.label: disrupt
v5.why: ‘Disrupt relations’ means to interrupt them harmfully — a negative action.

v6.label: encourage
v6.why: ‘Encourage relations’ means to promote them — a positive action.

v7.label: establish
v7.why: ‘Establish relations’ means to set them up — a positive action.

v8.label: foster
v8.why: ‘Foster relations’ means to encourage and support them — a positive action.

v9.label: improve
v9.why: ‘Improve relations’ means to make them better — a positive action.

v10.label: jeopardise
v10.why: ‘Jeopardise relations’ means to put them at risk — a negative action.

v11.label: maintain
v11.why: ‘Maintain relations’ means to keep them going well — a positive action.

v12.label: promote
v12.why: ‘Promote relations’ means to actively support them — a positive action.

v13.label: restore
v13.why: ‘Restore relations’ means to repair them after damage — a positive action.

v14.label: resume
v14.why: ‘Resume relations’ means to start them again after a pause — a positive action.

v15.label: sever
v15.why: ‘Sever relations’ means to end them completely — a negative action.

v16.label: sour
v16.why: ‘Relations sour’ means they turn bad — a negative development.

v17.label: strengthen
v17.why: ‘Strengthen relations’ means to make them stronger — a positive action.

v18.label: undermine
v18.why: ‘Undermine relations’ means to weaken them — a negative action.

g1.label: 1. Impolite staff ___ the reputation
g1.why: ‘Damage the reputation’ is the standard collocation; ‘disrupt’ doesn't fit reputation.

g2.label: 2. Planning to ___ branch offices
g2.why: ‘Establish branch offices’ is the standard collocation for setting up offices.

g3.label: 3. Greatly ___ our sales force
g3.why: ‘Greatly’ signals a big change, which fits ‘strengthened’, not ‘maintained’ (no change).

g4.label: 4. Relations ___ by poor service
g4.why: Poor after-sales service would harm relations, not foster them.

g5.label: 5. We are ___ relations with suppliers
g5.why: A new communications system would improve, not sour, relations.

g6.label: 6. A strike ___ production
g6.why: A strike disrupts production; it doesn't resume it.

g7.label: 7. We ___ talks regarding a joint venture
g7.why: ‘Broke off talks’ is the standard idiom for ending negotiations.

g8.label: 8. Success was ___ by a poor campaign
g8.why: An unimaginative campaign would put success at risk, not cement it.

g9.label: 9. We are ___ relationships with local agents
g9.why: Gaining market share requires building relationships, not cutting them off.

g10.label: 10. Relations ___ by official visits
g10.why: Official visits and trade delegations encourage relations, they don't sever them.

m1.label: 1. Rumours of a hostile takeover bid are certain...
m1.why: This pairs with ‘to strain relations between the two leading French software companies’.

m2.label: 2. The Accounts Department's slow payment...
m2.why: This pairs with ‘is causing stormy relations with some of the company's suppliers’.

m3.label: 3. The long-term contracts...
m3.why: This pairs with ‘have cemented relations between the two companies’.

m4.label: 4. The excellent relations with the local community...
m4.why: This pairs with ‘are a credit to its highly effective PR Department’.

m5.label: 5. As a result of currency controls...
m5.why: This pairs with ‘its close relations with several major foreign investors have been jeopardised’.
